text: Karibu! Ten African nations are at the FIFA Under-Seventeen World Cup in Qatar. Here is how to see their best young players first.
This is the Afritech Sports Tournament Desk. It is built for clubs, agents and federations, so you see the players who matter early, with a clear recommendation on each.
Africa holds ten of the forty-eight places. We cover every African squad, from the first match to the final on the thirteenth of December.
Start with the results. Every African match, with the goals, the key numbers, and a full match report. Senegal beat Cuba nine-nil.
As one reader told us: This desk works well for me, because of the match links.
Then the board. Seventy-three players to watch, forty-one of them African. Each card gives a clear call for clubs, agents and federations, and what would move him up or down.
All ten African squads in one view. Every kick-off in Doha time, the same as Nairobi. And the desk reads in English, French, Kiswahili and Portuguese.
Every rating rests on FIFA's official video, and tells you how far to rely on it.
The group stage ends on the twenty-seventh of November. If you are recruiting at this World Cup, book a briefing. Email Advisory at afri-tech sports dot com.
